title: Hypnos: Memory Efficient Homomorphic Processing Unit
problem: FHE accelerators traditionally use Host+ACC topology assuming encrypted data already resides on-chip, neglecting PCIe bus inefficiency and memory access overhead; this leads to poor end-to-end performance dominated by data movement rather than computation.
method: Hypnos abstracts FHE operators into memory-efficient commands and combines them with a homomorphic encryption paged memory management system, significantly reducing memory access and execution time through intelligent data staging and on-chip cache hierarchy optimization.

title: PacQ: A SIMT Microarchitecture for Efficient Dataflow in Hyper-asymmetric GEMMs
problem: Weight-only quantization for LLMs stores weights in low-precision INT format while activations remain full-precision FP. During execution on SIMT architectures, weights must be unpacked and dequantized back to FP before GEMM, negating compute efficiency gains.
method: PacQ co-optimizes INT weight packing and dataflow strategies at tile-level, then designs a specialized FP-INT multiplier unit enabling parallel processing of multiple INT weights. The microarchitecture integrates packing, optimized dataflow, and custom multiplier into a SIMT design.

title: SpecMPK: Efficient In-Process Isolation with Speculative and Secure Permission Update Instruction
problem: Memory Protection Keys (MPK) enable user-space access control for in-process isolation, but the permission update instruction (WRPKRU) is serialized, imposing significant performance overhead when applications require frequent domain switches to enforce isolation of critical data and pointers.
method: SpecMPK speculatively executes the MPK permission update instruction (WRPKRU) out-of-order rather than serializing it. A lightweight microarchitecture enhancement monitors all subsequent memory instructions that follow a speculative permission update: any instruction that would access a memory region whose permission was transiently upgraded (i.e., a potential speculative access to protected data) is blocked from committing until the permission update instruction itself becomes non-squashable (i.e., past the point of no return in the ROB). This prevents transient permission upgrades from being exploited by speculative execution attacks while allowing the processor to overlap permission update latency with useful computation.

title: RpcNIC: Enabling Efficient Datacenter RPC Offloading on PCIe-attached SmartNICs
problem: RPC processing has become a dominant datacenter tax in microservice/serverless environments, but existing RPC accelerators either integrate logic into the CPU or use specialized low-latency interconnects unavailable in commodity servers, preventing broad deployment.
method: RpcNIC is a software-hardware co-designed SmartNIC on Xilinx U280 FPGA using three techniques to mitigate PCIe overhead: (1) a target-aware deserializer that batches cross-PCIe writes on SmartNIC SRAM using compacted hardware data structures to reduce PCIe transaction count; (2) a memory-affinity CPU-SmartNIC collaborative serializer that trades host memory copies for slow PCIe transfers, keeping data on the host side for NUMA-affine access; and (3) an automatic field update mechanism that dynamically reconfigures RPC kernel schema encoding to minimize redundant PCIe traversals when application schemas change.

title: 36.1 A 32Gb/s 10.5Tb/s/mm 0.6pJ/b UCIe-Compliant Low-Latency Interface in 3nm Featuring Matched-Delay for Dynamic Clock Gating
problem: Dynamic clock gating in chiplet interconnects introduces instantaneous current surge (Di/Dt) and supply voltage droop when transitioning from gated to ungated modes, causing data sampling misalignment and bit errors.
method: A 32Gb/s, 64-lane UCIe module implements matched-delay architecture to manage clock gating transitions. Matched delays maintain synchronized clock-to-data timing even during mode transitions by compensating voltage droop-induced delay variations. The architecture ensures stable sampling windows and prevents data errors from Di/Dt-induced droops.

title: A 64Gb/s/wire 10.5Tb/s/mm/Layer Single-Ended Simultaneous Bi-Directional Transceiver with Echo and Crosstalk Cancellation for a Die-to-Die Interface in 28nm CMOS
problem: Die-to-die (chiplet) interfaces demand ultra-high edge density and low BER; simultaneous bi-directional (SBD) signaling doubles data rate but introduces echo (near-end reflection) and crosstalk (NEXT/FEXT). Existing echo-cancellation circuits are power-hungry; removing ground shielding for density gains increases crosstalk vulnerability.
method: Single-ended SBD transceiver with integrated analog echo cancellation (EC), near-end crosstalk (NEXT), and far-end crosstalk (FEXT) cancellation. Shield-less channel design (ground shielding removed). Three-layer cancellation approach: EC suppresses echo from local transmitter; NEXT/FEXT cancellation handles coupling from aggressor wires on same die.

title: GEM: GPU-Accelerated Emulator-Inspired RTL Simulation
problem: CPU-based RTL simulators face scalability bottlenecks; FPGA emulators are expensive and inaccessible; prior GPU acceleration fails due to heterogeneous circuit partitions conflicting with SIMT parallelism.
method: GEM introduces a virtual Very Long Instruction Word (VLIW) architecture inspired by FPGA emulator design, optimized for CUDA execution. The circuit logic is mapped to the VLIW architecture via a CAD flow analogous to FPGA place-and-route, mitigating irregular memory access patterns and thread divergence that prevented prior GPU simulators from achieving speedup.

title: A 12A 89.3% Peak Efficiency and 26mV Undershoot 12-to-1V Two-Stage Converter with Regulated Resonant Switched-Capacitor Regulators
problem: Power converters for data centers and processors require large output current (12A) at sub-1V supply voltages, while achieving high efficiency, low undershoot, and fast transient response across wide voltage ranges (12V to 1V).
method: Two-stage regulation architecture: an intermediate bus converter (IBC) steps 12V to intermediate voltage with high efficiency, followed by a switched-capacitor point-of-load converter with regulated resonant operation achieving 89.3% peak efficiency and 26mV undershoot.

title: RAP-Track: Efficient Control Flow Attestation via Parallel Tracking in Commodity MCUs
problem: Control flow attestation (CFA) for safety-critical embedded systems requires remote verification of program execution paths, but current approaches suffer from high performance overhead due to code instrumentation and frequent context switches.
method: Leverages commodity hardware extensions—Micro Trace Buffer (MTB) and Data Watchpoint and Trace Unit (DWT)—to track control flow paths in parallel with program execution, avoiding instrumentation overhead and context switches. Implements prototype on open-source systems.

title: LEGOSim: A Unified Parallel Simulation Framework for Multi-chiplet Heterogeneous Integration
problem: Simulating heterogeneous multi-chiplet systems (e.g., CPU+GPU+CIM chiplets integrated on an interposer) is not supported by existing simulators (gem5, GPGPU-Sim) because they lack modular composition of heterogeneous chiplet models and suffer from prohibitive synchronization overhead in parallel simulation—per-cycle global synchronization can waste up to 99.9% of simulation time on barrier overhead.
method: LEGOSim wraps individual chiplet simulators (open-source or proprietary) as parallel OS processes called 'simlets', each advancing independently using a PDES (parallel discrete event simulation) approach. An on-demand synchronization protocol uses adaptive time quanta and non-global fencing: synchronization only occurs when a simlet needs to send or receive a message whose timestamp falls within another simlet's current quantum, avoiding unnecessary global barriers. A Network-on-Interposer (NoI) simulator models inter-chiplet communication (latency, bandwidth, topology) and is integrated as a separate simlet. The framework was validated against SIMBA (multi-chiplet neural network accelerator) and a CiM-based accelerator, achieving average errors of 3.79% and 3.94% respectively.

title: Rethinking Dead Block Prediction for Intermittent Computing
problem: Existing dead block predictors, designed for conventional always-on systems, are ineffective in energy-harvesting intermittent computing systems because they do not account for power failures that invalidate cache blocks before they can be reused, causing unnecessary leakage energy waste on blocks that are nominally 'live' but will be lost.
method: EDBP (Enhanced Dead Block Predictor) augments existing dead block predictors with a power-failure-aware prediction layer. It identifies cache blocks that, though predicted live by a conventional predictor, are unlikely to be accessed before the next anticipated power failure. These blocks are deactivated (gated off) to eliminate leakage energy, freeing energy budget for forward execution. EDBP is combined with the Cache Decay predictor to achieve near-theoretical-minimum cache leakage across 20 Mediabench and MiBench applications.

title: Neoscope: How Resilient Is My SoC to Workload Churn?
problem: Hardware lifetimes are increasing while software workloads evolve rapidly, so SoCs optimized for today's workloads may perform poorly against future workloads; architects lack quantitative tools to design for long-term performance resilience.
method: Neoscope introduces two workload-change metrics, Magnitude and Disruption, that quantitatively characterize how a workload evolves over time, classifying churn as Minimal, Perturbing, Escalating, or Volatile. Using these metrics, Neoscope formulates SoC design space exploration as an integer linear program (ILP) combined with job-shop scheduling concepts, enabling it to find near-globally-optimal SoC configurations for a given churn span in a single invocation rather than requiring exhaustive parameter sweeps. The framework is multi-objective and can optimize simultaneously for performance, area, energy, cost, and carbon efficiency.

title: Blaze: An Efficient Bit-Sparse Attention Architecture With Workload Orchestration Optimization
problem: Attention mechanisms have high computational complexity and power consumption in NLP models; existing bit-sparsity methods focus on CNNs and don't address workload imbalance and hardware under-utilization caused by irregular distribution of non-zero bits in attention tensors.
method: Blaze combines value-level and bit-level sparsity exploitation with workload orchestration optimization. It proposes an Approximate-Computing-Based (ACB) workload orchestration mechanism to mitigate load imbalance from irregular non-zero bit distributions. Additionally, a Leading-Booth mechanism enhances bit-serial computation. The design includes a reconfigurable computing engine supporting both mechanisms.

title: I-DGNN: A Graph Dissimilarity-based Framework for Designing Scalable and Efficient DGNN Accelerators
problem: Dynamic Graph Neural Network (DGNN) execution requires passing each graph snapshot through the entire DGNN pipeline from layer to layer, generating excessive intermediate data and off-chip memory access, even when consecutive snapshots differ only slightly.
method: I-DGNN proposes a one-pass DGNN computing model that extracts graph update as a chained matrix multiplication between evolving graphs through rigorous mathematical derivation, decoupling inter-snapshot computation from the full DGNN pipeline and expressing it as an independent kernel. A unified accelerator architecture is dynamically configured to support the computation characteristics of this model, providing improved data and pipeline parallelism. A new dataflow and mapping tailored to I-DGNN improves data locality for inter-kernel data across the DGNN pipeline. The framework reduces intermediate data movement across layers.

title: PCcheck: Persistent Concurrent Checkpointing for ML
problem: Checkpointing large ML training runs to persistent storage introduces high overhead when done at high frequency, yet infrequent checkpointing leads to long recovery times after failures — a growing problem as training scale increases and cheap spot VMs dramatically raise failure rates.
method: PCcheck introduces persistent concurrent checkpointing, where model parameter checkpoints are taken concurrently with ongoing training (overlapping checkpoint I/O with compute) while also ensuring persistence to durable storage. It uses a combination of copy-on-write snapshots of model state and pipelined multi-stage I/O to overlap CPU-to-storage transfers with GPU computation. The system tracks consistency across concurrent training steps to guarantee that the checkpoint captured is valid and recoverable, minimizing pause time during the checkpoint process.

title: 14.3 A 28nm 17.83-to-62.84TFLOPS/W Broadcast-Alignment Floating-Point CIM Macro with Non-Two's-Complement MAC for CNNs and Transformers
problem: Floating-point neural network inference requires high precision but incurs significant energy/area overhead vs. integer quantization; floating-point CIM (compute-in-memory) faces challenges: (1) alignment operations conflict with CIM's parallel structure, (2) peripheral alignment circuits add area/power, (3) 2's-complement MAC wastes cycles on negative-weight sparsity and sign-bit overhead.
method: Broadcast-Alignment (B-A) floating-point CIM macro with embedded lightweight convertor for BF16/INT8 MAC operations. Broadcast input + embedded adaptive-alignment scheme with dual-bit serial MAC. Non-2's-complement (N2CMAC) MAC format reduces dynamic circuit activity and sign-bit overhead. Format-mixed approach supports BF16 and INT8 in same macro.
